bug_semantics: A privileged attacker can persist a custom RSE attribute whose key or value contains HTML/JavaScript. When another authenticated user opens the RSE-management detail page, get_rse_attributes receives that server-provided attribute and the renderer concatenates item and data[0][item] into an HTML string passed to jQuery's $() and append(). The browser therefore parses attacker-controlled data as markup instead of text, producing stored XSS in the WebUI origin; JavaScript can read exposed WebUI tokens/non-HttpOnly cookies and act with the victim's session.
flaw_origin: Commit 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735 introduced the RSE detail UI as new files. In lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js, new get_rse_attributes code at original lines 29-43 fetched persisted attributes and, at lines 39-40, interpolated the attribute key and value directly into a <tr> HTML string before appending it to #t_rse_attributes. Commit bf34d5206808923bc31091b0c5254a838e30e148 later extracted the same unsafe lines into create_attributes_table, but its parent already contained the vulnerable inline renderer, so that refactor is not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names author and committer Hannes Hansen <hannes.jakob.hansen@cern.ch>, contains only the subject 'WebUI: added support for getting informations, creation and deletion of RSEs and attributes Fix #80', and has no body, Co-Authored-By trailer, Generated-with trailer, bot identity, or other AI marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/rucio/rucio/security/advisories/GHSA-fq4f-4738-rqxm (CVE-2026-25736) identifies the create path Admin > RSE Management > RSE > Add Attribute, the trigger path Admin > RSE Management > RSE, an accepted POST /proxy/rses/WEB1/attr/XSS payload, and affected/patched boundaries <35.8.3/35.8.3, >=36.0.0rc1,<38.5.4/38.5.4, and >=39.0.0rc1,<39.3.1/39.3.1.

History proof: `git blame -L 29,50 4176e7a34b239f46325e4553e6a1b7bb36fbdd26 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js` attributes the inline get_rse_attributes callback and the unsafe append expression to 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735. `git show 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js lib/rucio/web/ui/templates/rse.html` shows both files created from /dev/null and the vulnerable lines added. Commit URL: https://github.com/rucio/rucio/commit/8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735.

Direct-parent proof: `git ls-tree -r --name-only c77904c15e1958ad9f32e862b9e9714e48076434 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js lib/rucio/web/ui/templates/rse.html` returns no entries. Thus the RSE page, its get/list path, and the vulnerable HTML interpolation are absent from the BIC's immediate parent tree.

Refactor exclusion: `git log -L 29,34:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js 24468abb0e076fa83d5f3bc6db6050182fed4c79^` leads to bf34d5206808923bc31091b0c5254a838e30e148, but `git show bf34d5206808923bc31091b0c5254a838e30e148` shows it merely moved the already-unsafe inline append from get_rse_attributes into create_attributes_table; its parent 4176e7a34b239f46325e4553e6a1b7bb36fbdd26 still has the vulnerable expression and blame resolves it to 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735.

Fix proof: upstream direct commit https://github.com/rucio/rucio/commit/fce81437e2e647a0da6e348167ea1df26db87c0c, parent 91c4303fcdc76a143150dcf20b5bd6a138b4adad, is titled 'fix(WebUI): fix XSS using jQuery.append', explicitly names GHSA-fq4f-4738-rqxm, and changes lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js create_attributes_table from an interpolated HTML string to separately created elements whose key, value, and button text are inserted with jQuery .text(); this removes HTML parsing of attribute data.

Release-backport proof: patch-id 8048d8a0027a38f9af84df71029df645b337e325 is identical for upstream fce81437e2e647a0da6e348167ea1df26db87c0c and branch commits 24468abb0e076fa83d5f3bc6db6050182fed4c79, e8848dfc66f79e5cc9d1077ef371d971dd290db1, and 1559c59e1fc571f75775fb4f656d752b32309e24. `git for-each-ref --contains` shows those three backports respectively absent from 35.8.2, 38.5.3, and 39.3.0 but present in exactly the patched tags 35.8.3 (ba9203702629af7bb1f95d5cf9ba8fcf1f943105), 38.5.4 (c851ad216e0e0e3d50405eab3331dfe21c96ddd3), and 39.3.1 (ba2a7e66b1e3c73b5cf9e0000e6621e8dc45bfe7). First-party release URLs: https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/35.8.3, https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/38.5.4, and https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/39.3.1.

Affected-range ancestry: `git for-each-ref --contains=8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735` confirms the BIC is an ancestor of boundary/start tags 35.8.2, 35.8.3, 36.0.0rc1, 38.5.3, 38.5.4, 39.0.0rc1, 39.3.0, and 39.3.1. The first release-line check shows 1.17.8 does not contain the BIC while 1.18.0 (643e022b0d20232c0ca62b4efbfb239244c63996) does, placing the vulnerable feature in released history years before the affected modern branches.

BIC-only attribution proof: `git cat-file -p 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735` shows tree d1ea89ffb346f8e9414aa6cf092706d17c4cc1a7, sole parent c77904c15e1958ad9f32e862b9e9714e48076434, human author/committer Hannes Hansen with the same CERN email, and the single subject line; there are no trailers, additional message text, signatures, bot identities, or AI-attribution markers. No later commit or fix attribution is used for the verdict.
reasoning: The advisory's stored-XSS path maps directly to the custom-attribute callback in rse.js: persisted attacker input returns through list_rse_attributes and is converted into executable DOM because the renderer constructs HTML rather than text nodes. The earliest causal code is not the 2018 helper extraction found by a superficial -L trace; inspecting that commit's parent reveals the same vulnerable inline renderer. Blame and the creation diff take the lineage one step earlier to single-parent commit 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735, and its direct parent lacks both relevant files, proving absence. The BIC is a normal, non-squash commit, so no decomposition is applicable. Upstream fix fce81437e2e647a0da6e348167ea1df26db87c0c replaces string interpolation with DOM construction plus .text(), and byte-equivalent patch backports land precisely in all three advisory patched tags while their immediate prior boundary tags lack them. The BIC predates and is ancestral to every modern affected branch checked. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has only a human CERN author/committer and no AI marker; under BIC-only attribution this is a closed NOT_AI result.
